entity.name: Ajnas N B
entity.description: I am an independent Indian open-source maintainer and the primary maintainer of Qarinah. I built it after repeatedly watching coding agents lose project decisions, replay large histories, and hand work between tools without durable evidence. I design and maintain the implementation, releases, evaluations, documentation, security process, and community roadmap. My goal is to make reliable, portable project memory a shared open-infrastructure primitive that developers can run locally, inspect, extend, and integrate without depending on a hosted memory account.

projects.name: Qarinah
projects.description: Qarinah is Apache-2.0, local-first project-memory infrastructure for coding agents. It retains permitted project events in an append-only, hash-chained JSONL ledger and builds deterministic SQLite/FTS5, graph, Markdown, and dashboard views that can be deleted and rebuilt from that authority. Its CLI, JavaScript API, and consent-gated MCP transport compile bounded context packs with citations, provenance, freshness, authority, and coverage information instead of replaying an entire project history. The public project also includes cross-agent setup, archive import and backup, schemas, interoperability formats, a responsive local dashboard, reproducible evaluations, and security and privacy documentation. This grant will strengthen its security, interoperability, cross-platform releases, independent reproducibility, beginner onboarding, contributor path, and long-term maintenance capacity.

plans.name: Qarinah six-month public reliability and adoption roadmap
plans.description: Six-month, outcome-based public roadmap. M1 — Baseline and participation: publish the funded roadmap as tracked issues with acceptance criteria; document the release, security, privacy, and benchmark baselines; improve the contribution guide; and publish the first community progress update. M2 — Interoperability: publish a versioned specification, schemas, conformance fixtures, and compatibility tests for the event ledger, context packs, CLI, JavaScript API, and MCP integrations. M3 — Reproducible releases: verify clean installs and pinned-package interoperability on Linux, macOS, and Windows; document the release process; and publish CI and artifact receipts that an external maintainer can reproduce. M4 — Independent security and privacy review: commission an external assessment, triage every finding, remediate confirmed issues, and publish an appropriate report or advisory with the resulting security-response process. M5 — Independent evidence and onboarding: commission reproduction of the scoped public benchmarks; publish methods, results, limitations, and machine-readable receipts; and release a beginner-focused demo repository and installation path. M6 — Community and sustainability: complete small contributor bounties, publish maintenance and incident-response playbooks with response targets, hold a second public community review, and publish final outcomes and spending reports. Budget: INR 240,000 for maintainer engineering, specifications, and release work; INR 120,000 for the independent security and privacy assessment; INR 60,000 for cross-platform and reproducible-release infrastructure; INR 60,000 for independent benchmark reproduction; INR 60,000 for beginner onboarding and the demo repository; INR 30,000 for contributor bounties; and INR 30,000 for maintenance and security-response capacity. Success means an external contributor can install Qarinah on all three supported desktop operating systems, verify the public specification and release evidence, reproduce the published benchmark fixtures, follow a documented security path, and make a first contribution. All funded deliverables, reports, specifications, fixtures, and code will be public.
